title: Code Editor
description: Public API, language-aware indentation, key row, follow mode, synchronisation, accessibility, and native platform behaviour for Firstlight Code Editor.

runs.text: Code Editor edits plain-text configuration and code — JSON, YAML,
files, and plain text — in a monospaced native text view with line numbers, language-aware indentation, and a key row above the software keyboard. It has no syntax highlighting.

NativePHP publishes at most 64 KB of props for one element, so the value must stay under about 60 KB of UTF-8. Larger content throws a contract exception instead of reaching the device as an empty editor. For live logs, keep only the newest lines. Public Blade examples use kebab-case. Code Editor always turns off autocorrect, autocapitalization, and spell checking, and uses the system monospaced font at the platform's text size.
Return keeps the current line's leading spaces or tabs. In
adds one level, and Return between a bracket pair splits it onto three lines. Typing
at the start of a line removes one level. In
, Return after a line ending in
adds one level; comments are ignored.
Indent and Outdent act on the current line or every selected line. Toggle comment, in
on the current or selected lines. Indentation always inserts spaces; existing tabs are kept.

blocks.text: While the field is focused and editable, a key row sits above the software keyboard. It is hidden when a hardware keyboard is attached, where Tab and Shift-Tab indent and outdent.

While the field is focused, the native buffer, cursor, selection, IME composition, scroll position, and undo history stay local. PHP acknowledgements do not replace them. Unfocused programmatic updates replace the text, clear undo history, and never emit

blocks.text: A programmatic update never jumps to the top. The first visible line stays in place when lines are appended or removed from the start, and otherwise the previous scroll offset is kept.

runs.text: , the view starts at the end and stays there across updates while it is within one line of the end, including when PHP trims the start of the content. Scrolling up stops following; scrolling back to the end resumes it. While a person holds a selection in a read-only editor, updates wait until the selection collapses so copying is never interrupted. Updates are not announced to VoiceOver or TalkBack.

is required during development. Line numbers are hidden from assistive technology, so validation messages should quote the offending key or content rather than only a line number. Every key-row key has an accessible name and meets the 44 pt / 48 dp target. Code text stays left-to-right in right-to-left layouts.

content often contains secrets. Code Editor is not a secure field: it does not mask values, block screenshots, or guarantee that keyboards skip learning what is typed. Decide whether editing secrets on the device is acceptable for your application.
